exact_source_operations.old: Uncountability and being residual are independent properties: $\mathbb{Q}$ is meager and countable, the Cantor set is meager and uncountable ([[thm-cantor-set-properties]]), and $X$ is residual and uncountable.
exact_source_operations.new: Residuality implies uncountability for subsets of $\mathbb{R}$, but uncountability does not imply residuality: $\mathbb{Q}$ is meager and countable, the Cantor set is meager and uncountable ([[thm-cantor-set-properties]]), and $X$ is residual and uncountable. Indeed, every countable subset of $\mathbb{R}$ is meager by the singleton argument in step 1.1 (with the empty set represented by an all-empty sequence). A meager set cannot also be residual: its union with its meager complement would make $\mathbb{R}$ meager, contradicting [[thm-baire-category-r]].

exact_current_citation.quote:
Write $\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}$ for the image of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\mathbb{R}$
under the canonical embedding $q \mapsto \hat q$ ([[lem-rat-embeds-dense]]), the
set usually written $\mathbb{Q}$ once the identification is made, and put
$X := \mathbb{R} \setminus \mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}$ for the irrationals. Then:

1. $\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}$ is an $F_\sigma$ set ([[def-f-sigma-g-delta]]) and is
   meager ([[def-nowhere-dense-meager]]);
2. $X$ is a $G_\delta$ set and is residual;
3. $\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}$ is **not** a $G_\delta$ set, and $X$ is **not** an
   $F_\sigma$ set.

Claims 1 and 2 are bookkeeping. Claim 3 is the substance and is exactly where
[[thm-baire-category-r]] is spent: no argument from the algebra of open and
closed sets alone can reach it, since $\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}$ and $X$ are
interchanged by complementation while $F_\sigma$ and $G_\delta$ are, so any such
argument would prove the same thing about both sets and about neither.

mathematical_disposition.defect: False two-way independence assertion: residuality entails uncountability in R.
mathematical_disposition.smallest_prerequisite: Real singletons are nowhere dense (current proof 1.1); a nonempty countable set has a surjective N-enumeration; empty set is meager; two meager sets have a witnessed interleaved union; Baire says R is not meager. All are already local or read proved suppliers.
mathematical_disposition.argument: If S is countable, enumerate its singletons (or use the all-empty sequence), so S is meager. If S were also residual, R minus S is meager by definition; union of these two explicit meager presentations gives R meager, contradicting Baire. Thus residual S is uncountable. The Cantor set is uncountable and meager, hence not residual by the same union contradiction, so the converse fails.
mathematical_disposition.scope_preserved: Retains the original three Statement conclusions, entire phase proof and all examples in the Remark. Retains the independent elementary proof of irrational uncountability and strengthens the explanatory relation to the correct one-way implication.
mathematical_disposition.proof_interface_followthrough: No change to Facts, Statement, Definition, phase proof or dependency list is necessary; the short justification lives in the corrected Remark and uses existing local 1.1 and existing category/Baire deps.
mathematical_disposition.choice: Only one enumeration and one witnessing meager complement sequence are fixed; merging two sequences is explicit. No countably infinite family of meager witnesses is selected and no new choice hypothesis is introduced.
